canonicalName: Set-theoretic measurable coloring meets distributed local algorithms

milestones.label: Measurable Lovász local lemma
milestones.work: A. Bernshteyn, Measurable versions of the Lovász Local Lemma and measurable graph colorings, arXiv:1604.07349 (2016)
milestones.description: Measurable coloring tools precede the explicit distributed-algorithm transfer.

milestones.label: Distributed-to-descriptive transfer stated
milestones.work: A. Bernshteyn, Distributed Algorithms, the Lovász Local Lemma, and Descriptive Combinatorics, arXiv:2004.04905 (2020)
milestones.description: The public paper states that efficient finite-graph local algorithms can yield well-behaved Borel-graph colorings.
milestones.note: The same paper states and applies the transfer.

milestones.label: Randomized local algorithms yield measurable colorings
milestones.work: A. Bernshteyn, Distributed Algorithms, the Lovász Local Lemma, and Descriptive Combinatorics, arXiv:2004.04905 (2020)
milestones.description: The paper applies randomized LOCAL algorithms to measurable and Baire-measurable coloring problems.

evidence.claim: The abstract explicitly states the measurable-coloring application

milestones.note: The same paper truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

milestones.label: Homomorphism graphs link descriptive and distributed methods
milestones.work: S. Brandt et al., On Homomorphism Graphs, arXiv:2111.03683 (2021)
milestones.description: A later paper adapts descriptive-combinatorial methods to the distributed LOCAL model.

works.citation: Distributed Algorithms, the Lovász Local Lemma, and Descriptive Combinatorics

notes: The inherited citation 'Rozhon et al., ITCS 2022' was too vague to assign a work record. arXiv:2111.03683 is On Homomorphism Graphs, a related later development, not Bernshteyn's founding transfer. No dedicated named institution was verified.

canonicalName: Non-rationality of cubic fourfolds attacked via mirror-symmetry-inspired Hodge atoms

milestones.label: Iritani's quantum-cohomology blowup theorem
milestones.work: H. Iritani, Quantum cohomology of blowups, arXiv:2307.13555 (2023)
milestones.description: The later Hodge-atoms paper explicitly says its blowup behavior accords with this theorem.
milestones.note: This work concerns blowups, not a cubic-fourfold irrationality proof.

milestones.label: Hodge atoms and cubic-fourfold result posted
milestones.work: L. Katzarkov, M. Kontsevich, T. Pantev and T. Y. Yu, Birational Invariants from Hodge Structures and Quantum Multiplication, arXiv:2508.05105 (2025)
milestones.description: The public preprint introduces Hodge atoms and states irrationality for very general cubic fourfolds.

evidence.claim: Version 1 was public in August 2025 and contains this claim

milestones.note: The same preprint states the framework and applies it; the claim is for very general cubic fourfolds.

milestones.label: Hodge atoms obstruct rationality
milestones.work: L. Katzarkov, M. Kontsevich, T. Pantev and T. Y. Yu, Birational Invariants from Hodge Structures and Quantum Multiplication, arXiv:2508.05105 (2025)
milestones.description: The authors apply the new invariants to prove that a very general cubic fourfold is not rational.

evidence.claim: Version 1 explicitly states and proves the very-general-cubic-fourfold result

milestones.note: The same preprint truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

works.citation: Birational Invariants from Hodge Structures and Quantum Multiplication
Birational Invariants from Hodge Structures and Quantum Multiplication
Birational Invariants from Hodge Structures and Quantum Multiplication
Birational Invariants from Hodge Structures and Quantum Multiplication

notes: The source claims irrationality only for a very general complex cubic fourfold, not every cubic fourfold. The catalogue's 2019 conceptual date had no checked work and is not promoted. Iritani's 2023 work is a precursor to blowup behavior, not the proof itself.

canonicalName: Machine learning guides conjectures in knot theory and representation theory

milestones.label: Nature paper sets out machine-learning-guided discovery
milestones.work: A. Davies et al., Advancing mathematics by guiding human intuition with AI, Nature 600 (2021)
milestones.description: A public article describes a workflow that uses learned patterns and attribution to guide mathematical conjectures.

evidence.claim: Published Nature research article in December 2021

milestones.label: Knot signature–cusp relation proved
milestones.work: A. Davies, A. Juhász, M. Lackenby and N. Tomašev, The signature and cusp geometry of hyperbolic knots, arXiv:2111.15323 (2021)
milestones.description: A machine-learning-discovered relation leads to a proved knot-theoretic inequality.

milestones.label: Kazhdan–Lusztig candidate formula
milestones.work: C. Blundell et al., Towards combinatorial invariance for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, arXiv:2111.15161 (2021)

Towards combinatorial invariance for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials

notes: The catalogue's 2019 date has no checked public work for this particular paired application and is not promoted. The companion preprints were posted in November 2021, just before the Nature article in December; within-year ordering matters for any claim of a single first publication.

canonicalName: AlphaTensor: reinforcement learning for matrix multiplication algorithms

milestones.label: Strassen's faster matrix multiplication
milestones.work: V. Strassen, Gaussian elimination is not optimal, Numer. Math. 13 (1969)
milestones.description: A classical faster algorithm is the benchmark later surpassed for particular small matrices.

milestones.label: AlphaTensor research article
milestones.work: A. Fawzi et al., Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with reinforcement learning, Nature 610 (2022)
milestones.description: The published paper describes a reinforcement-learning game for exact matrix-multiplication tensor decompositions.
milestones.note: The same article introduces and applies AlphaTensor.

milestones.label: AlphaTensor finds improved multiplication algorithms
milestones.work: A. Fawzi et al., Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with reinforcement learning, Nature 610 (2022)
milestones.description: The agent finds exact decompositions, including a 4×4 mod-2 algorithm using 47 multiplications.

evidence.claim: The article reports the 4×4 finite-field result

milestones.note: The same paper truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

milestones.label: Kauers–Moosbauer improve a mod-2 record
milestones.work: M. Kauers and J. Moosbauer, The FBHHRBNRSSSHK-Algorithm for Multiplication in Z₂^{5×5} Is Still Not the End of the Story, arXiv:2210.04045 (2022)
milestones.description: An independent search rapidly improves a finite-field multiplication record.

works.citation: Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with reinforcement learning

notes: AlphaTensor concerns discovery of exact algorithms; the result is not a general improvement to the asymptotic matrix-multiplication exponent. Fawzi's personal research page identifies his role and links the work.

canonicalName: Integer distance sets via the determinant method

milestones.label: Anning–Erdős integral distances
milestones.work: N. H. Anning and P. Erdős, Integral distances, Bull. AMS 51 (1945)
milestones.description: A classical paper establishes an earlier structural restriction on infinite integral-distance sets.

milestones.label: Greenfeld–Iliopoulou–Peluse post structural theorem
milestones.work: R. Greenfeld, M. Iliopoulou and S. Peluse, On integer distance sets, arXiv:2401.10821 (2024)
milestones.description: The public preprint states that nearly all points of a planar integer-distance set lie on a line or circle.
milestones.note: The same paper states and proves the target structural result.

milestones.label: Determinant method applied to integer-distance structure
milestones.work: R. Greenfeld, M. Iliopoulou and S. Peluse, On integer distance sets, arXiv:2401.10821 (2024)
milestones.description: The authors use the determinant method to cover lifted points by curves and derive structural and diameter bounds.

evidence.claim: Section 1.4 explicitly uses the determinant method to cover lifted points by algebraic curves

milestones.note: The same paper truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

notes: The determinant-method step is stated explicitly in section 1.4 of the original paper. Anning–Erdős 1945 is a precursor, not the new structural theorem.
